# Fact Grain

The grain of a fact table is the answer to "what does one row mean?". It is the first decision in a
[[star-schema]], because every later choice — which dimensions can attach, which measures are
additive, which duplicates are impossible — follows from it.

## Declare it, then enforce it

[[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] states the grain in prose **and** makes the primary
key carry it, in both marts:

| Mart | Grain | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|
| Retail sales | one row per sales order line | PK on the source order-line identifier |
| Price quotes | one row per ticker per trading day | composite PK `(TickerKey, DateKey)` |

> "The primary key states the grain: one row per ticker per trading day. A fact table without one
> leaves the grain to be inferred from the loading query, which is how duplicate rows get in."
> — Data-Warehousing-and-Business-Intelligence/project/twtr/sql/02_star_schema.sql, 2026-07-25

The point of that comment is that a grain written only in documentation is a comment; a grain written
as a primary key is a constraint the database enforces on every future load. It is the same instinct
as [[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]] applied at DDL time rather than at load time, and the same
instinct as [[idempotent-loading]] — uniqueness lives in the schema, not in the loader.

## Consequences that show up immediately

- **Measure additivity.** At order-line grain, `LineTotal` sums freely across any dimension. At
  ticker-day grain, a closing price does not sum across days at all — which is part of why an
  indicator computed over a window is not a stored dimension attribute, see [[measure-vs-dimension]].
- **Which dimensions can attach.** A dimension can only join if it is meaningful at the grain. A
  salesperson is meaningful per order line; it is also frequently absent, hence
  [[nullable-salesperson-key]].
- **Window functions need the grain to be regular.** The whole `ROWS BETWEEN n PRECEDING AND CURRENT
  ROW` construction in [[window-function-frames]] assumes one row per ticker per trading day and
  silently means something else if that stops being true.

## Grain outside the warehouse

The same discipline shows up in [[labour-fraud-analysis]], where the twenty-table dataset is
FK-closed and each table's row count is reconciled against a committed manifest — a row-count
reconciliation is only meaningful if you can say what one row is. See [[third-normal-form]] and
[[reproducible-analysis]].
